issues.legal_issue: An administrative determination cannot rest on grounds outside the grounds stated in the notice that initiated the proceeding.
material_facts: The notice called on the affected persons to show cause only on the basis of one stated category of evacuee status.
The authority ultimately declared them evacuees under two additional categories that the notice had not identified.
The appellate authority found the stated ground vague and the notice defective to that extent.
issues.conclusion: The declaration under the categories not identified in the notice was invalid because the inquiry and determination went beyond the notice.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 7 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, a valid notice is the foundation of the proceeding. An inquiry that travels beyond the bounds of the notice is impermissible and without jurisdiction to that extent. No earlier cases are relied on for this principle.

predicates.property_status_declaration_proceeding: An authority conducts a proceeding to determine whether a person or property has a regulated status.
predicates.notice_identifies_limited_basis: The authority's notice tells the affected person that the proceeding rests on a specified, limited basis.
predicates.final_determination_adds_unnoticed_basis: The authority's final determination relies on a basis that the notice did not identify.

issues.definition: When a status-determination proceeding is based on a notice stating a limited basis, a determination that adds an unstated basis is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A notice initiating an administrative proceeding is invalid if it fails to state the factual grounds with enough particularity to allow the affected person to answer the case.
material_facts: The notice reproduced the prescribed form's general wording but supplied no particulars about the alleged acquisition of an interest in evacuee or abandoned property.
The notice did not explain the factual basis of the allegation, and the appellate authority described the stated ground as very vague and the notice as defective to that extent.
issues.conclusion: The notice did not comply with the applicable notice requirements and could not provide a valid foundation for the subsequent proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, requires notice before an inquiry and declaration. Rule 6(1) of the Administration of Evacuee Property (Central) Rules, 1950, governs service of notice where the authority is satisfied that property is prima facie evacuee property; rule 6(2) requires the notice, as far as practicable, to state the grounds and the relevant category of alleged evacuee status. The factual particulars are essential to enable the affected person to answer the case. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.property_status_declaration_proceeding: An authority conducts a proceeding to determine whether a person or property has a regulated status.
predicates.notice_states_only_general_allegation: The authority's notice gives only a general allegation rather than the specific factual basis for the proposed determination.
predicates.notice_omits_answerable_factual_particul: The notice leaves out factual details needed for the affected person to understand and answer the allegation.

issues.definition: In a status-determination proceeding, a notice that gives only a general allegation and omits answerable factual particulars is invalid, as are proceedings founded on it.

issues.legal_issue: An authority may not initiate a property-status proceeding without forming the required preliminary opinion on a basis supported by material available to it.
material_facts: A prior proceeding concerning whether the affected person was an intending evacuee had been dropped after no reliable evidence was found to support that status.
On the same day, the authority initiated a proceeding to declare the person and property evacuees.
The record contained no material showing that the authority then had evidence supporting initiation of the new proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The notice appeared to have been issued without any basis, and the notice and subsequent proceedings were invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, required the Custodian to form an opinion that the property was evacuee property before taking action. Rule 6(1) of the Administration of Evacuee Property (Central) Rules, 1950, required the Custodian to be satisfied from information in his possession or otherwise that the property was prima facie evacuee property before issuing notice. The Court also relied on the absence of material on the record to support the authority's initiation of the proceeding. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.property_status_declaration_proceeding: An authority conducts a proceeding to determine whether a person or property has a regulated status.
predicates.prior_related_status_case_dropped_for_la: The authority previously dropped a related status proceeding after finding no reliable evidence to support it.
predicates.new_notice_issued_without_supporting_mat: The authority issued a notice initiating a new proceeding without material supporting the proposed determination.

issues.definition: In a status-determination proceeding, if a related case was dropped for lack of reliable evidence and a new notice is issued without supporting material, the notice and proceedings founded on it are invalid.
